To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the hierarchical approach to web content classification is superior to the non-hierarchical approach, (2) the hierarchical approach can be used in conjunction with flat non-hierarchical classification to further improve the performance, and (3) the performance of the hierarchical approach can vary significantly depending on the quality of the hierarchy.

(i) hierarchical classifiers can be trained to achieve higher performance than flat classifiers, (ii) the hierarchical classifiers can be used to classify web pages into a large number of second-level categories with high accuracy (83%), and (iii) a hierarchical classifier can be trained to identify a second-level category with high accuracy (85%) using only a few examples.
